# Resolvio

Resolve ENS profiles, cryptocurrency addresses, text records, and content hashes over HTTP. Reverse-resolve Ethereum addresses to verified ENS primary names. No API key is required for public reads.

Base URL: https://api.resolvio.xyz
Documentation: https://docs.namespace.ninja/user-guide/resolvio
API reference: https://docs.namespace.ninja/api-reference/resolvio/get-ens-profile
Full machine-readable reference: https://resolvio.xyz/llms-full.txt
Agent skill: https://resolvio.xyz/skill.md
OpenAPI JSON: https://api.resolvio.xyz/api-docs.json

## Choose an endpoint

- Profile: `GET /ens/v2/profile/:name?texts=avatar&addresses=eth&contenthash=false`
- Address records: `GET /ens/v2/addresses/:name?chains=eth,base`
- Text records: `GET /ens/v2/texts/:name?keys=avatar,description`
- Content hash: `GET /ens/v2/contenthash/:name`
- Reverse lookup: `GET /ens/v2/reverse/:address`
- Reverse profile: `GET /ens/v2/reverse/:address/profile`
- Bulk profiles: `GET /ens/v2/profile/bulk?names=vitalik.eth,nick.eth`
- Bulk reverse: `GET /ens/v2/reverse/bulk?addresses=...`
- Supported chains: `GET /ens/v2/chains`

## Parse responses

Profile `texts` and `addresses` are arrays. Text records contain `key`, `exists`, and optional `value`. Address records contain `coin`, optional `chain`, `exists`, and optional `value`. Contenthash is `{ exists, value? }`, not a string. Match by key or coin type, and check `exists` before reading values.

Bulk profiles return an array. Bulk reverse returns an object with an `addresses` array. Single reverse results have `hasReverseRecord` and an optional `name`. Reverse profile results instead use explicit null fields when there is no verified primary name.

## Parameters and defaults

Use `addresses` for profiles, `chains` or `coins` for the addresses endpoint, and `keys` for the texts endpoint. There is no `useDefault` API parameter. Omitted profile selections use server defaults; empty lists do not disable record groups. Set `contenthash` explicitly.

The default bulk cap is 20. Default cache durations are 300 seconds forward and 1800 seconds reverse, configured by the operator. They do not come from an onchain TTL. `noCache=true` requests a refresh but may reuse recent entries where a refresh cooldown is enabled. Do not treat it as a guarantee of an uncached read.

For complete parameters, missing-record behavior, and errors, read the full reference above.
